ai_assessment.method: Full direct Bengali-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 68 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported 2 major and 20 minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.425; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then obtained a second fresh separate-context assessment of the revised text (8.825, minor findings only), applied its fixes, and assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: The শ্বশুরবাড়ি jail euphemism was lost; Rahamat, arrested with tied hands, now answers “Thì đang đi nhà chồng đây nè!”, letting the double meaning surface through the scene without an in-text gloss.
Rahamat’s broken Bengali had been rendered as fluent native Vietnamese; now marked by Babu, salaam, tui and small grammatical slips, with a deliberate shift to tôi after prison.
মারিতাম is conditional (‘I would hit him’): Tui đánh bố chồng liền, mà làm sao được — tay bị trói rồi.
The needless চন্দ্রবিন্দু joke rendered with a needless Vietnamese tilde: “Või!”.
The sixteen-anna pun is carried in the wording (đáng giá trọn cả đồng rupi mười sáu anna) rather than an explanation.
মঙ্গল-আলোক contrasted with the forgone electric lights: thứ ánh sáng của phúc lành.

summary: Full assessment of all 68 Bengali/Vietnamese passages and both titles. Mini’s chatter, the arrival of the Kabuliwala, the raisins and the half-rupee, the jokes about the bag and the father-in-law’s house, the stabbing and arrest, the years of forgetting, the wedding day return, the handprint of Rahamat’s own daughter and the narrator’s gift are complete and in order. The first separate-context pass scored the draft 8.425 (below threshold) with two major findings; after revision a second fresh pass scored 8.825 with only minor findings, which were then applied. Fidelity, naturalness, imagery and mechanics are 9.0, voice 8.5 because Rahamat’s foreignness is only lightly marked. Unrounded weighted score 8.875 meets the unchanged 8.6 threshold. No unresolved major or critical issue remains.

title_review.rationale: Người Kabul names Rahamat as the narrator and the household see him, a man from Kabul; it keeps the body term and avoids the peddler’s trade suffix -wala, which has no neat Vietnamese equivalent.
